Product illustration vocabulary

Three things carry these: the person, the ground behind them, and UI kept to a hint. Twenty-eight grounds and five glass treatments below, then nineteen compositions built the way the references are — on our palette, with our people, in Nunito Sans.

Grounds

All from the tokens, all carrying a fine grain. Tonal singles for most cards. Rises when the card should stand in the colour and bleed off the bottom. Blends run into a deep end — Tide is sky into our own teal. Spans run sideways. Blooms and painterly grounds layer several soft lights over a blend; those are what the references actually use behind a person.

Glass

Five treatments for a card on a ground. Solid is the default. Frost when a second card sits behind the hero. Rim is a white card wearing a translucent border that lets the ground through. Halo rings the card in soft white light — the reference's dialog. Tile is the floating satellite.

Solid
Solid — the default
Frost
Frost — 72% white, 20px blur, 1px light rim
Rim
Rim — 6px translucent border, ground shows through
Halo
Halo — 10px white glow ring, plus a soft drop
Tile — 68px satellite, glass, soft shadow

Compositions

Each is one reference's construction, rebuilt with our people, our product and our grounds. Pick one, change the person, the moment and the hue. A–F came first; G onward are built from the second set of references.

S · Agenda + detail — a list behind, one item pulled forward

The rules that make it one system

RuleWhy
A person is the largest thing in the cardAvatar 84–96px, a photo tile taking a third of the card, or an arch portrait breaking the frame edge. The UI names the feature; the person is the reason to look.
One hue per illustrationGround, tinted controls, accent bar and button gradient all share it. A second hue is the fastest way off-system.
UI is a hintOne title, one line of meta, skeleton lines for anything longer, at most one button. The app shell and device are the exception — they crop the real product at two edges rather than shrink it.
Every ground carries grainA fractal-noise overlay at 13–16%, blended overlay. It is most of the difference between a CSS gradient and artwork.
Radii: frame 28 · card 24 · photo 16 · controls 12 · device 40 · pills 9999One step softer than the site's own, so illustrations read as artwork.
Glass has four jobsFrost for a card behind the hero; rim for a white card on a deep blend; halo for a dialog that needs lifting off a busy ground; tile for a satellite. Solid otherwise.
Bleed one edge when the card is standing in the colourRises, glass splits, shells and devices crop. Tonal singles usually don't.
Nunito Sans, ladder sizes, no shadow on the flat card24/18/16/14/12. 600 only on titles and buttons. Shadows belong to satellites, devices and the halo.
